name: Tribhuvan International Airport
before:
Nepal's only international airport, and the starting point for most Everest trips. Several flights a day run to Lukla for trekkers, and sightseeing flights along the Himalaya leave from here too.

It connects Kathmandu to more than forty destinations across seventeen countries, with Nepal Airlines and Himalaya Airlines both based here alongside the domestic carriers.

Two things to build into an itinerary. The airport is running at capacity, and winter fog and congestion cause real delays, to the point that the government has promoted the newer airports at Gautam Buddha and Pokhara as diversion alternatives. And the apron is tight: it takes seventeen aircraft at once but only three of those can be wide bodies, with a further bay on the eastern side.

The runway is a tabletop, built on raised ground that falls away at the ends, which is worth knowing for a nervous flyer. Domestic and international operations run from separate terminals.
after:
The airport for Kathmandu, and no longer Nepal's only international airport: Gautam Buddha at Bhairahawa and Pokhara are international airports too.

Flights to Lukla for Everest treks leave from here, though Tara Air, which flies the route, also sells Lukla flights from Ramechhap. Everest sightseeing flights leave early in the morning from the domestic terminal. Domestic and international flights use separate terminals.

claims.note: Was 'Nepal's only international airport', which the old text itself contradicted by naming Gautam Buddha and Pokhara as diversion airports. claims.claim: Held back: every Nepali airline is on the UK Air Safety List
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing in the old text (the airline sentence it would sit beside is cut). The FCDO (read 24 September 2026) says no Nepali airline currently meets international safety standards, so all are on the UK Air Safety List and banned from flying to or from the UK, and that Nepal has had a number of fatal air accidents, with at least 100 deaths in the last five years.
